newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says cabinet announcements not far off.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says cabinet announcements not far off.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday he would announce new Cabinet members for his second term before "too long."

Speaking to reporters after an Oval Office ceremony honouring astronaut Shannon Lucid, Clinton said he was not ready to announce members of his national security team, including the secretaries of state and defence and his national security adviser.
"When I have an announcement I will make it," Clinton said. "I expect to work hard this week and I'll be making some announcements as they're ready to make. It won't be too long."
Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry are among many Cabinet members who have announced their intentions of leaving at the end of Clinton's first term.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton discussed appointments with senior officials on Monday and thinking on the new national security team was "fairly well advanced."
Clinton, still suffering from hoarseness that developed on his recent Asian trip, said he had spent the past four days resting at the Camp David presidential retreat.

"You can hear that my voice is better, but not fully recovered," Clinton said. "I took four days off with my family, indeed, my extended family ... It's the longest time I've had off without any work in more than a year.
"I'm trying to do a little work and found I simply couldn't make telephone calls. And so, I had four days off," he said.
